statement: The truncation trunc c f (min over B of f(B) + c|A minus B|) is the largest potential below f with increments at most c; it equals f at A iff the Edmonds/Nash-Williams inequality holds at A; if f has increments at most c it equals f everywhere (counting case).

Necessity of the payment Hall condition for arbitrary monotone unit-increment rank functions: pairwise disjoint full parts give the split condition for the sum and the count sum r_w(A) <= |A|. No matroid axiom.

Diagonal and counting: the flipped diagonal is explicit and needs one private point per device (at most as many devices as points); halving names a missed function for fewer than 2^m devices on m points at the price of a count over devices per point; pigeonhole gives existence only.

Views (equivalence relations) embed in families of properties (viewOf (famOf r) = r); any two families containing every singleton have the same view; if every one-string language is in P (hypothesis) then P and NP induce the same view of strings.
The rank of three parallel payers is monotone, submodular, unit-increment, violates monogamy of mutual information, and is the min-cut function of no weighted network.

On the 21 stored circuits (PHC at point 0, Lemma D potential, all 621,808 payer subsets): split condition holds 21/21; unit truncation submodular, 0 violations; largest one-gate jump of the potential between 2 and 6; monogamy of mutual information violated by the potential in 13 circuits (293 of 3,982 triples) and by its truncation in 2.
CKW monogamy is not the payment Hall condition: CKW is a constraint on every state (the counterpart of the trivial half of PHC), PHC is an existence statement; payment ranks are not monogamous.
